references.text: The immediate context: God commands Noah to take seven pairs of every clean animal into the ark, an instruction that is expanded to include birds in the next verse.
God gives the first instruction to bring two of each kind into the ark. Later, this is expanded to seven pairs for clean animals and birds, to enable sacrifice and preservation of the species.
God blesses the birds and commands them to be fruitful and fill the earth – the same purpose underlying their preservation through the flood.
After the flood, God commands that all animals be released from the ark to be fruitful and multiply on the earth, fulfilling the purpose of their preservation.
Noah offers sacrifices from the clean animals and birds after the flood, which explains why it was necessary to take seven pairs – not just two – of the birds.
God refers to Noah's flood and His promise never again to flood the earth, a covenant made possible because Noah preserved all life through the flood.
Direct narrative connection: Specification of the number of bird pairs (7 pairs) as an exception to the general rule of two pairs in 6:19.
Narrative context: Elaboration on the categories of animals to be brought into the ark to preserve life.
